Patient Name: [Redacted]

Date of Discharge: [Redacted]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
History of Present Illness:
The patient, a 10-year, 10-month-old male neutered Shih Tzu, was admitted for further examination of a peracute onset of lethargy and left-sided circling. The general physical examination was normal. Neurological examination revealed circling to the left, decreased proprioceptive positioning of the right thoracic and pelvic limbs, and a decreased menace response on the right side. Routine hematology and serum biochemistry were normal. Urine-specific gravity, urine chemistry dipstick analysis, sediment examination, and urine culture were all unremarkable. Assessment of NIBP using Doppler identified a systolic pressure of 170 mmHg. Fibrinogen, PT, aPTT, and D-dimer were all within normal limits. TEG analysis revealed a shortened R time and SP on citrated plasma. MRI scan of the brain under general anesthesia showed an extensive intra-axial, focal, well-demarcated lesion affecting the cerebral gray matter extending from the left frontal lobe to the rostral aspects of the left temporal lobe. The lesion was T2W and FLAIR hyperintense compared to normal gray matter and T1W hypointense. There was evidence of mild mass effect, and there was no contrast enhancement.

Hospital Course:
The patient was closely monitored, and no underlying cause for the ischemic stroke could be identified. The dog improved with time and was discharged from the hospital 72 h after admission. The dog made a near to full recovery within 14 days and was neurologically normal at re-assessment five months later.

Medications:
N/A

Follow-up Care:
None necessary at this time.

Signed,
[Physician Name]

# Principal diagnosis: **I63.9 – Cerebral infarction, unspecified**

**Important caveat:** This patient is a dog (a 10-year-old Shih Tzu). ICD-10-AM is a human classification used for Australian hospital morbidity coding, so it does not formally apply to veterinary patients. Veterinary records usually use systems such as SNOMED CT (veterinary extension) or VeNom codes. The code below is the closest human equivalent, for academic or mapping purposes only.

## Why I63.9

- **Condition:** The summary states this was an **ischaemic stroke**. The MRI showed a focal, well-demarcated intra-axial lesion in the left frontal and temporal gray matter. It was T2W/FLAIR hyperintense, T1W hypointense, and did not enhance, which fits an infarct rather than a tumour or haemorrhage.
- **No cause identified:** The summary explicitly says "no underlying cause for the ischemic stroke could be identified." So the more specific I63.0–I63.8 codes, which require a known thrombotic, embolic, or occlusive cause, are not supported.
- **Artery not named:** The lesion's location suggests the middle cerebral artery territory. However, no vessel occlusion is documented, so I63.5 (occlusion/stenosis of cerebral arteries, unspecified) would be inferring beyond the record.

## Possible additional codes (if mapping)

| Finding | Possible code | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Systolic BP 170 mmHg | R03.0 (elevated BP reading without diagnosis of hypertension) | Hypertension was not diagnosed |
| Hypercoagulable TEG (shortened R time and SP) | R79.8 / D68.8 | Only if the clinician documents it as a clinically significant thrombophilic state |
| Neurological deficits (circling, right-sided proprioceptive deficits, reduced menace) | Not coded separately | These are part of the stroke |
